scenes.title: 1997 UC Irvine PET Imaging Suite: 41 Matched Brain Scans Reveal the 'Missing Frontal Brake' — Plus the 1998 Impulsive vs Planned Twist!
scenes.era: 1997–1998, Brain Imaging Center, University of California, Irvine

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1997 university neuroimaging viewing gallery featuring a sleek circular **medical PET scanner gantry** in the background and a bright **4-Panel Lightbox Display** comparing **Healthy Control (Warm Active Frontal Pole)** vs **Impulsive Offender (Dim Frontal Brake)** vs **Planned Offender (Normal Frontal Activity!)** vs **Non-Violent Professor With Safe Childhood (Buffered Outcome!)**.

positions.who: Adrian Raine (mannequin in 1997 British-academic tailored suit and tie)
positions.where: standing at the illuminated 4-panel PET lightbox pointing from the dimmed frontal lobe of the Impulsive subgroup across to the intact Planned subgroup and the Biosocial Protection chart

positions.who: Monte Buchsbaum & Neuroimaging Fellow mannequins (in crisp white clinical lab coats)
positions.where: comparing the 41-vs-41 matched Continuous Performance Task data sheets with clean museum-grade scientific rigor

props.name: 4-Panel Illuminated Brain Metabolism Lightbox (Control | Impulsive Low-PFC | Planned Normal-PFC | Safe-Home Buffer)
props.period_detail: tells BOTH the famous 1997 finding AND the essential 1998 anti-determinism twist in one clean frame

props.name: 41-vs-41 Matched FDG-PET & Biosocial Interaction Stand
props.period_detail: shows biology × childhood environment interaction clearly

actions.verb_sequence: places the 41-vs-41 matched PET axial maps onto the bright lightbox -> highlights dimmed prefrontal braking in the Impulsive group -> places the 1998 Planned (Normal-PFC) and Safe-Childhood Professor scans right beside it to shatter 'born criminal' determinism!

reactions.reaction: leans in stunned that Planned offenders had normal frontal fuel AND peaceful professors carried similar scans
underscores: 'Vulnerability is NOT destiny — childhood care changes the ending!'

scenes.wardrobe: 1997 California medical-research attire: tailored charcoal suit and tie; crisp white laboratory coats over collared shirts.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key clinical gallery daylight balanced with crisp illuminated viewing panels.
scenes.recognition_hook: In 1997, PET scans of 41 homicide defendants revealed dimmed prefrontal brakes — then one year later, splitting Impulsive from Planned offenders AND scanning two peaceful professors blew 'born bad' myths wide open!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1997 UC Irvine neuroimaging gallery where Adrian Raine stands at a 4-panel PET brain-scan lightbox comparing Control, Impulsive low-frontal, and Planned normal-frontal scans before clinical researchers

layout.description: Bright seminar gallery with two translucent 3D brain models contrasting Affective/Impulsive (low PFC + hot amygdala) vs Predatory/Planned (intact PFC + high subcortical drive).

positions.where: demonstrating why executive planning requires intact prefrontal glucose

props.name: Affective vs Predatory Subgroup Chart (1998)
props.period_detail: explains heterogeneity hidden inside group averages

actions.verb_sequence: splits the 41-scan average into two distinct neural profiles

reactions.reaction: confirm there is NO single 'offender brain'

scenes.recognition_hook: Average 41 scans together and you miss half the story — separate hot-tempered impulse from cold planning and frontal metabolism splits down the middle!
